summary: Revision 3 extends the explorer and launcher already shipped in revisions 1 and 2 rather than adding a new subsystem. R9 adds a plain, testable file-operation core beside the existing one-level lister (src-tauri/src/features/explorer/ops.rs) with four thin, async commands; they reuse the editor Store by adding one additive repath method so open tabs follow renamed or moved files, and reuse the editor's existing close/bin behaviour for deleted tabs after the UI snapshots unsaved text. The sidebar panel keeps its existing tree and open path and gains toolbar/row actions, a dialog for create/rename, the existing pickFolder for an explicit Move, and HTML5 drag-and-drop onto folders. R10 is a CSS-only change to the command palette: mobile-first base rules plus a desktop media query, no component or package change. R11 adds one serde-default-true executable field to the Rust and TypeScript terminal models, filters start_all, stop_all and engine `up` with one AppDef helper, and filters the existing rollup/appButton call sites in App, AppHeader, HomeScreen and Sidebar; EditPane gets one labelled toggle and new terminals default true. R12 is mostly verification plus adding F5 where a Start all / Stop all hint is shown (palette entries and the app header); refresh keeps no shortcut and no F5-refresh wording. Scale and resources: every operation touches one item and refreshes only the affected folder level(s) under the existing 1,000-row/10,000-scan caps; no new cache, poller or listener is added, FS work runs on spawn_blocking, the trash crate is the only new dependency, filtering is a linear pass over one app's terminals at render time (no new memo needed), and the palette change is a static CSS media query with no runtime cost. Version 2.2.0 is bumped together in package.json, Cargo.toml and tauri.conf.json.

additions.title: Show that a file operation is working or failed
additions.why: A slow or refused create, rename, move or delete must not look like nothing happened.
acceptance: While an operation runs the explorer shows a busy state and its action controls are not double-fired.
When an operation fails or is refused, a clear message names what could not be done and the affected folder is reloaded from disk.

additions.title: Check a name and destination before touching any file
additions.why: An empty, illegal or clashing name, or a folder moved inside itself, must be refused without changing anything.
acceptance: An empty, whitespace-only or Windows-invalid name is refused with a message and nothing is created or renamed.
A destination that already exists is refused and the existing item is left byte-for-byte unchanged.
Moving a folder onto itself or into one of its descendants is refused before any file-system call.

additions.title: Keep the saved editor index pointing at renamed or moved files
additions.why: A tab must still open the same file after its path changes, and it must still be there after a restart.
acceptance: Renaming or moving an open file updates its saved editor path and title without losing its unsaved buffer.
Every open file under a renamed or moved folder is re-pointed in the saved index.
The affected tab ids and new paths are returned so the window and the tab groups agree immediately.

additions.title: Snapshot unsaved text before closing a deleted item's tab
additions.why: Deleting a file whose tab has unsaved typing must keep that text in the editor bin rather than losing the last keystrokes.
acceptance: Closing the tabs of a deleted item first writes any pending typing snapshot, then closes each tab.
A tab with unsaved text ends in the editor bin with its latest text; a clean tab is forgotten as before.

additions.title: Say when there is nothing executable to start
additions.why: When every terminal is non-executable, pressing Start all or F5 must explain why nothing started instead of looking broken.
acceptance: Pressing Start all or F5 on an app whose terminals are all non-executable starts nothing and shows a brief No executable terminals message.
The message is dismissible and leaves every terminal and the current view as they were.

additions.title: Keep the three version numbers in step
additions.why: The desktop build must report one version everywhere it is installed or packaged.
acceptance: package.json, src-tauri/Cargo.toml and src-tauri/tauri.conf.json carry the same bumped version.
